sources.purpose: Current dated official FOMC target-range decision and dissent verification
sources.reliability_limits: This statement establishes the target range and vote on October 28, not the effective federal funds rate or a prediction of future policy; verify later FOMC releases before treating it as current.

learnings.title: October 28 FOMC holds 3.75%-4.00% by 10-2; distinguish dated target from effective rate
learnings.claim: On 28 October 2026, the Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold the federal funds target range at 3.75%-4.00%; Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack preferred a 25-basis-point increase. This supersedes the September 16 release as the latest dated FOMC policy decision, but does not itself establish the effective federal funds rate.
learnings.decision: FED_FOMC_20261028_CURRENT_PRIMARY_GATE: In the next Finance decision/report, cite the October 28 official statement for the latest target range (3.75%-4.00%) and the 10-2 vote; distinguish the two dissenters' preference for a 25bp hike from the actual hold. Do not present the September 16 decision as the latest; verify newer statements at execution time. For effective-rate analysis require separately dated H.15 or equivalent primary observations. Record this learning ID in the actual Finance decision/report applied_learning_ids only when the gate changes or validates that real output.
learnings.next_measurement: Find the actual Finance report/decision artifact produced after October 28 and verify the dated target range, vote, explicit latest-release check and applied_learning_ids; add a negative test rejecting stale September-only headline and missing source.
fallback_history: If the official latest FOMC release is unreachable, mark current decision freshness unverified and do not infer a hold or hike from forecasts.
Preserve the September 16 historical learning and its source; do not delete or rewrite historical records.
